extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and reporters learning types of news writing
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook-style collection of exemplar news reports illustrating how to cover legislative actions, municipal meetings, conventions, clubs, and social gatherings; intended to teach reporters different forms and tones of news writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal/legislative bill report
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the legislative maneuvering around a bill: who introduced it, committee referrals, motions to return or refer, committee votes, and the political motives behind support or opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'William R. Handy... succeeded in keeping the Justice of the Peace bill in the Committee on Municipal Corporations after the House had voted to request that committee to return the bill...'; include sponsor (John C. Harrison), committee membership, objections (Handy objected), motions (Harrison offered a motion that the committee be instructed to return the bill), committee action (voted to refuse the request and to retain possession). Also report political context and motives: labor of ward politicians, Democrats' electoral concerns, 'The controlling motive of the opposition... is the danger of breaking up the organizations through which political bosses are able to reward faithful henchmen.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative content and provision summary
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering a bill, summarize its substantive provisions and practical effects: electoral method, jurisdiction, qualifications, salaries, staffing, and administrative arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of provisions to state explicitly: 'Justices of the Peace shall be elected at large...each shall have jurisdiction throughout the city'; salary levels ('$3000 a year'); reduction in number (from 11 to 7); qualification requirements ('must be a licensed attorney'); clerk/constable provisions and pay ('One clerk...Constable...$2500 a year', deputies '$1800 a year each', plus fees '2½ per cent of all amounts collected'). Also note logistical provisions (rooms/offices, central location).

rubrics_metrics.name: City council meeting / ordinance report
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe ordinances introduced: author, purpose, route or scope, timeline and approval steps, franchise/financial terms, technical specifications, referral to committees, and political reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: identify ordinance and introducer ('introduced in Common Council yesterday by Peter E. Costello'); state route and stations (detailed station list); construction and approval timetable ('work shall be started within six months after the plans have been approved...'); franchise compensation ('pay to the city 10 per cent of its net profits...'); fare limits ('rate of fare is not to exceed 5 cents'); technical specs ('overhead clearance of 14 feet'); and committee referral ('referred to the Committee on Street Railways'). Include reactions from officials and stakeholders and whether the measure conflicts with other plans ('might seriously hamper the projects of Director Taylor').

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention/meeting report with expert statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover conventions and professional meetings by reporting notable presentations, experimental claims or findings, practical demonstrations or techniques, and elected officers or organizational actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: report speaker and affiliation, their claim and basis ('Dr. Louisa Burns...said...the action of the pulse...was influenced chiefly by the change of emotions' and 'drawn her conclusions from a long series of experiments'); include illustrative procedure or technique ('When a patient comes to my office I always find it is better to work with him as he lies on a table...I have found his pulse'); list other papers/presentations and elected officers ('These were elected officers...W. A. Merkley...President').

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety council / professional resolution reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting a safety or industry council meeting, note adopted resolutions, practical remedies, statistical evidence, recommended public-education measures, and remarks blaming or crediting parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: quote resolution language and commitments ('the members pledge themselves to the elimination of the use of alcoholic stimulants among the employes'); report practical remedies or programmes (buttons, swimming pools as youth diversion); cite safety statistics attributed to organizations ('for the year ending June 30, 1914, there had been 109 fewer deaths...and 132 fewer injuries'); include calls for educational campaigns ('The inculcation of accident prevention should start in the kindergarten and continue through high school and college').

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention committee recommendations (technical/public-utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize committee findings and recommendations on technical or public-utility matters: health and comfort (ventilation, lighting), service levels (schedules), sanitation (drinking water), billing practices, claims handling, and equipment standards, including suggested regulatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example recommendations to report: ventilation concerns ('More deaths are caused by improper ventilation of train coaches...'); lighting improvements ('vigorous campaign against...dingy, dirty oil lamp'); sanitary drinking-water measures (avoid stationary coolers, provide portable containers and free sanitary cups); minimum Sunday service ('at least one train should operate in each direction'); billing/claims practices (abolish paying freight bills carrying manifest over charges; require interest on true claim amount); regulatory power requests ('interstate commerce commission be given full power to prescribe the character of equipment...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature/club meeting narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: For human-interest or club stories, use narrative devices: colorful lead, metaphors, vote tallies, quoted diagnoses or jokes, background history of the group, and a witty or poignant closing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example elements: comic-obituary framing ('The Social Workers' Club is dead. The end came peacefully...'); record vote counts and attendees ('On a roll call six voted to let it die. Four voted for resuscitation. The remaining 20 did not care enough to vote'); historical sketch of the organization's rise and decline; quoted opinions diagnosing causes ('not social', 'malnutrition and faulty assimilation'); and closing observations about surviving related groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnic/grassroots meeting reportage with vernacular quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering meetings of immigrant or street-trade groups, capture local color with dialect dialogue, descriptive scene-setting, the grievances, and the group's planned actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example technique: set the scene (location, sounds), report grievances and policy complaints (anti-noise enforcement impact on business), reproduce representative quoted speech including dialect/Yiddish for authenticity ('No more I must gif my calls...If so much as I gry...a bolisman he koms...and grabs my arm'); record planned follow-up (sending delegation to Commissioner Bingham, agreement to call softly). Also note economic claims ('business has fallen off at least 50 per cent, since the anti-noise order').

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious meeting / society report (quiet, reflective tone)
rubrics_metrics.description: For coverage of religious or fellowship meetings, emphasize atmosphere, ritual elements, readings/messages exchanged, themes (e.g., 'One for another'), and procedural actions (reading letters, adopting minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example approach: describe setting and mood ('soft stillness...old, buff room Lighted only through the great, square-paned windows'); quote thematic lines or prayers ('Let us miss no opportunity of expressing the love we feel one for another'); note the meeting's business format (reading messages, resolutions called minutes, gentle approvals) and highlight notable international or intermeeting communications (messages from the London Meeting).
